entries.title: SDK update: load-agents

acceptedPr.title: Skip installed package directories when loading local agents
acceptedPr.author: Joonin81
acceptedPr.body:
## Summary
- Prune subdirectories that look like installed packages or checkouts (`package.json`, `node_modules`, or `.git`) during agent discovery, before importing them.
- Prevents vendored tooling and test entrypoints from running at startup and terminating the CLI (e.g. `process.exit()` in a pixelfx checker).
- Exposes `listLocalAgentFiles` so hosts can decide whether a repo-scoped `.agents` directory contains anything executable before importing it.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test sdk/src/__tests__/load-agents.test.ts` (40 pass, 0 fail)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` (pass)
- [x] Regression test: a `process.exit()` in a package subdirectory cannot terminate the loader

🤖 Generated with Codebuff

ai.title: SDK agent loader skips vendor directories
ai.summary: The SDK agent discovery in sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts now skips directories named vendor during local agent scanning, adding name === 'vendor' to the shouldSkipAgentDirectory predicate alongside existing exclusions like node_modules and scripts. This prevents third-party code installed under the shared ~/.agents/vendor directory by other tools from being imported and executed in the host process. The listLocalAgentFiles JSDoc was updated to document the new exclusion, and a regression test confirms that vendor subdirectories are pruned before import.
ai.evidence: The diff in sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts adds the vendor check to shouldSkipAgentDirectory and updates the JSDoc for listLocalAgentFiles, accompanied by a new test titled 'skips vendor/' that verifies files in vendor subdirectories are excluded from agent discovery.

eli5.text: The tool that finds and runs helper programs in your shared agent folder now ignores a specific subfolder where other software installs extra code. This stops any code placed there by outside tools from starting up automatically when you open your assistant. This is an internal safety update that prevents accidental program crashes, so you will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves during your daily use.
